summary: The bill amends the National Labor Relations Act to require employers and newly certified unions to begin bargaining within 10 days, refer unresolved first-contract disputes to mediation after 90 days, and submit them to binding arbitration by a three-person panel after 30 more days if mediation fails.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the NLRA to accelerate initial collective bargaining agreements via timelines, mediation, and binding arbitration. It contains no provisions authorizing, appropriating, or altering any federal expenditures.
No provisions address tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue collection.
The bill is silent on health insurance, coverage mandates, or healthcare delivery systems.
No references to firearms, background checks, or gun regulations appear in the text.
The legislation does not touch on visas, border enforcement, or immigration pathways.
No language relates to reproductive rights or abortion access.
The bill makes no changes to defense authorizations or military budgets.
Environmental regulations, emissions standards, or conservation measures are absent.
No provisions expand or contract welfare programs, SNAP, or other safety-net entitlements.
The bill does not address school funding, curriculum, or school choice.
No references to controlled substances, decriminalization, or enforcement appear.
The legislation contains no sentencing, policing, or criminal-procedure reforms.
Tariffs, trade agreements, and import/export rules are not addressed.
No fiscal measures affecting deficits or debt reduction are present.
The bill does not create, expand, or limit protections based on sexual orientation or gender identity.
Foreign assistance programs are outside the scope of this domestic labor bill.
No election-administration or voting-access provisions are included.
Data privacy, surveillance, or technology regulation are not mentioned.

The bill directly amends Section 8(d) of the NLRA to impose strict timelines for first-contract bargaining, mandatory mediation, and binding arbitration when parties fail to agree. These mechanisms are designed to strengthen unions' ability to secure contracts quickly and reduce employer leverage during delays, constituting a clear expansion of worker and union protections.
No provisions address religious exemptions or civil-rights enforcement.
